MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE
  Monday, June 7, 2021

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  temporarily suspends requirements  of the  Brown Act.  The Council Chambers was closed to the public, La Verne
  City Council Members attended this meeting telephonically, and meeting was live streamed on the City' s website.
2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6: 30 p. m.
3.  Council  Members  present:  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Muir Davis
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Interim Finance Director Mark Alvarado
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer

4.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Crosby.

  Community Events  check for any announcements via telephone communication.

  There was none.

Resolution No. 21- 27,  Resolution No. 21- 27- A Resolution OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY

Authorizing  a  Project List as  OF LA VERNE, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, And STATE OF CALIFORNIA
Required by Senate Bill 1, the  AUTHORIZING  A PROJECT LIST AS REQUIRED BY SENATE BILL 1: The
Road Repair Accountability Act  Road Repair and Accountability Act.

  In April 2017 Governor Brown signed  into law Senate Bill 1 ( SB1),  also

  referred to as the Road Repair and Accountability Act( RRAA) of 2017. SB1
  provides for increased gas taxes and registration fees, which are to be
  deposited into the State' s Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account
  RMRA). RMRA funds are apportioned to local agencies each year for basic
  road maintenance, rehabilitation, and other safety projects. SB1 also requires
  each eligible agency to submit a project list to California Transportation
  Commission ( CTC) in order to receive these funds. La Verne' s allocation for
  fiscal year 2021/ 22 is estimated  at$  570, 000.

  Public Works Director Igoe recommended approval of Resolution No. 21- 27,
  approving the proposed  SB1  project  list for fiscal year 2021/ 22. Approved as
  recommended.

  concluded. The Ordinance document required minor technical changes and

  Community Development Director Scherer recommends final approval of
  Ordinance No. 1098, adding a new Chapter 18. 94 to the La Verne Municipal to
  regulate the rental of residential property on short- term basis and amending
  related provisions. The Ordinance will take effect on August 17, 2021, when
  the current moratorium  expires.

8.  Discussion  Regarding City  Prior to discussion of this matter, City Manager Russi left the Zoom meeting.
  Manager Compliance  with
  Section 2. 04. 020 of the  City Attorney Kress reported on City Manager compliance with Section
  La Verne Municipal Code  2. 04. 020 of the La Verne Municipal Code regarding  residency.  He stated that

  Regarding Residency  Councilmembers Crosby and Lau are requesting that the City Manager be
  given finrelve months' notice to comply with the La Verne Municipal Code
  Section 2. 04. 020, which states that City Council require that the City Manager
  live in La Verne or within a 5- mile radius of City Hall. The Councilmembers are
  also requesting that during this compliance period the requirement be
  reviewed.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter.

  One ( 1) public comment  received  via phone communications.

  One ( 1) public comment via the webinar

  After discussion by the City Council on this matter, it was moved by Crosby,
  seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried by roll call vote to give the City
  Manager twelve months' notice to comply with La Verne Municipal Code
  Section 2. 04. 020 which provides that City Council require that the City
  Manager live in La Verne or within a 5- mile radius of City Hall; and that during
  the compliance period, the requirement be reviewed or be rescinded.

  The City Manager rejoined the Zoom meeting.

9.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other  place  on  the agenda.  Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via
  telephone  communication.

  Nine ( 9) public comments received via phone communications.

  Two ( 2) public comments received via the webinar

  To hear what was said during public comment, please visit the City' s website
  to view the archived Council meeting.

  Four( 4) public comments  received  via email ( attached).

  City Attorney Kress read a statement from former Interim Fire Chief Segura
  regarding Fire Departments services.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, June 7, 2021 , Page 5,

10.  Council  Comments  Councilmember Carder requested that discussion for support of a Vote of No
  confidence of Los Angeles County District Attorney George Gascon be placed
  on  the  next Agenda.  She spoke about the City hiring a Public Relations Officer
  in an effort to have transparency  and communication  in the comr unity. She
  stated that all five Council Members need to work together and to avoid the
  negativity.

  Councilmember Crosby commended the Department Heads for their budget
  presentations and that they did a great job.

  Councilmember Lau also thanked City staff for their great work on the budget.
  She reported on the Cultural Awareness and Social Inclusion ( CASI) meeting.
  She thanked the residents for their public comments. She urged residents do
  their homework on the COVI D- 19 vaccinations and to do what is best for them.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis spoke about the importance of discussion and keeping
  engaged within the community and City Council. He reported on the Cultural
  Awareness  and  Social Inclusion ( CASI) meeting  and urged residents to join.
  He stated there were many opportunities for residents to engage like joining
  the San Dimas/ La Verne Educational Committee  and  Foothill Transit. He

  urged residents to reach out to him by phone or text and he would be happy to
  meet with them.

  Mayor Hepburn reported on the San Gabriel Valley Council of Government
  COG) which he is the Vice- President and of their participation in supporting
  certain Senate Bills to help restaurants survive. He stated there are many
  diverse opinions and that the Fire issue is important to the community. He

  reportedthat on June 15 2021 , the County of Los Angeles would be reopened.
  He spoke about the upcoming events like Concerts in the Park, Movies in the
  Park, Fourth  of  July parade and fireworks  show.  He stated that he understood
  that the COVID- 19 Vaccination  is not for everyone, but urged residents to
  research and  do what is best for them.  He stated that the vaccination center at
  the Fairplex is closing.
